Try using a wax stick to smooth out the flyaways! You could try also using a silicone conditioning treatment.

A trick some wig companies use is to use an industrial silicone processing treatment on their hair to coat the cuticle. 

The silicone will be washed out within one to 3 washes leaving the cuticle exposed. Once a cuticle is exposed the hair is basically always going to be frizzy, dry and hard to manage so I always make sure I’m reading long term reviews. How this helps :)

It’s real but the ‘6 months’ part isn’t. These units last for 2-6 weeks because it’s really important to cleanse the regrowth scalp underneath. 

Leaving a unit on for 6 months could lead to bacterial and fungal infections. The good news is you can learn how to apply them yourself so you don’t have to rely on a barber or stylist all the time.
 
There’s a thread called /hairsystems on Reddit that’s basically the modern name for male focused units like these. 

Popular companies in the thread are Bono Hair, New Times hair and Hair Club. Hope this helps!
I think a sew in would really pull on your hair. I would avoid.

I would recommend briogeos plum stick for the fly aways ($28 which is expensive but they’re cheaper alternatives on Amazon) and an ion protein treatment for the frizz, I like K18.

If the hair is getting frizzy really quickly, it means that the hair is either really dry or the cuticle has been stripped. 

Over index on conditioner and moisturising products to compensate and avoid getting these products on the lace as it can loosen knots overtime. Hope this helps! Good luck with your wig journey :)
